title: loadConfig() fired in useEffect but AppShell renders immediately â€” children see null config on first render
detail: Line 225: `React.useEffect(() => { loadConfig(); }, []);` â€” the effect runs AFTER first render. NavPanel and SensorBanner both render in the same first paint and both call getEnvVar() during their render bodies (NavPanel:131, SensorBanner:32). On first render they see _configCache === null and getEnvVar returns null. NavPanel listens for the dcfg-config-changed event from reloadConfig() but loadConfig() does NOT emit that event â€” only reloadConfig() does. So the FIRST load never re-renders nav once config is in. SensorBanner doesn't listen for the event at all, so its kill switch (sensor_enabled='false') never engages. See CR-2026-04-09-0211 for the upstream portalApi side.
evidence: App.jsx:225 useEffect kicks loadConfig but does not await; portalApi.js:313-341 loadConfig does NOT dispatch the dcfg-config-changed event (only reloadConfig at line 348-354 does); NavPanel.jsx:99 listens for it; SensorBanner.jsx:30 does not.
recommendedFix: Change AppShell to gate AppRouter render on config-loaded state. Add `const [configLoaded, setConfigLoaded] = useState(false);` and `useEffect(() => { loadConfig().finally(() => setConfigLoaded(true)); }, []);`. Show the existing spinner until both `loading` and `configLoaded` are true. This is the cleanest fix and removes the race for every consumer at once. Alternatively, dispatch the dcfg-config-changed event from loadConfig() (not just reloadConfig) â€” smaller change but doesn't help SensorBanner unless it also listens.

title: AppRouter has zero RoleGuard wrappers â€” admin/internal routes accessible to any authenticated user
detail: AppRouter.jsx defines ~30 routes and not a single one is wrapped in <RoleGuard>. Admin-only paths (/admin, /flow-monitor, /send-queue, /absorption, /capital-plan) and internal-tool paths (/nora, /interview) are reachable by typing the URL hash, regardless of user role. The RoleGuard component exists in shared modules and is correctly built (RoleGuard.jsx); it's just never used in the router. NavPanel hides nav items via the nav_menu_{role} config pattern, but a user who knows the URL can bypass that entirely. For external customer-facing user testing, an external tester landing on /#/admin would see admin actions. Per CR-2026-04-09-0220, NavPanel ALSO doesn't role-gate properly â€” the two issues compound.
evidence: AppRouter.jsx:56-151 â€” every Route uses bare element prop, no RoleGuard imports. Compare to the existence of src/RoleGuard.jsx (which exports the component) and the JS-06/C-06 rule documented in usePortalUser.jsx:9 ('Actions the user cannot perform are REMOVED FROM THE DOM entirely').
recommendedFix: Wrap admin/internal routes in <RoleGuard require="admin">: e.g. `<Route path="admin" element={<RoleGuard require="admin" fallback={<Navigate to="/dashboard" replace />}><Admin /></RoleGuard>} />`. Apply to /admin, /flow-monitor, /send-queue, /absorption, /capital-plan minimum. The fallback should redirect non-admins to /dashboard rather than render null (otherwise the user sees a blank page with no explanation). Same pattern for manager-only routes (e.g. /onboarding/:id depending on rule). This is a coordinated change with CR-2026-04-09-0220 (NavPanel role logic).

title: apiPost has no return value but several callers treat it as if it returns the created record
detail: apiPost (line 159-164) is a void function â€” it throws on non-OK and falls off the bottom on success with no return statement. But several call sites in the SPA (notably LocationManager.jsx:555, see CR-2026-04-09-0201) await it and read `.dcfg_*id` off the result, which is always undefined. This is a contract bug in the shared API: either the function should return the parsed body / OData-EntityId GUID, or every consumer that needs the created record must use apiPostReturn. Currently the API has both apiPost (void) and apiPostReturn (returns record) and apiPostReturnId (returns just the GUID), but the naming is non-obvious â€” easy to grab the wrong one.
evidence: portalApi.js:159-164 â€” function body has no `return`. portalApi.js:166-188 apiPostReturn returns the record; portalApi.js:191-199 apiPostReturnId returns just the GUID string. LocationManager.jsx:555 uses apiPost expecting a record (see CR-2026-04-09-0201).
recommendedFix: Two-part fix: (1) audit every `apiPost(` call site across the SPA and confirm none of them read the return value (subagent task during Phase 5). (2) Add a JSDoc comment to apiPost making the void contract explicit: `/** Fire-and-forget POST. Returns void. Throws ApiError on non-OK. Use apiPostReturn() if you need the created record back. */` Optional Phase 5 enhancement: name the trio `apiPostVoid`, `apiPostReturn`, `apiPostReturnId` to make the contract obvious at the call site.

App.jsx kicks off loadConfig() inside a useEffect at boot, but several modules call getEnvVar() during their initial render â€” most importantly SensorBanner.jsx:32 (`if (getEnvVar('sensor_enabled') === 'false') return null;`) and NavPanel.jsx:131 (`getEnvVar(`nav_menu_${role}`)`) â€” meaning the first render of those components ALWAYS sees null and proceeds with default behavior (sensor banner enabled, nav menu showing all items). recommendedFix: Two complementary fixes: (1) Make App.jsx await loadConfig before rendering AppShell â€” show the spinner until config is loaded. This is a small render-order change in App.jsx and removes the race for everyone. (2) Have SensorBanner subscribe to the dcfg-config-changed event the same way NavPanel does, so kill-switch toggling at runtime works. Both changes are independent and safe.

title: useMemo dep array includes searchFields â€” inline-literal callers blow the cache every render
detail: Line 63: `}, [rows, sortCol, sortDir, searchTerm, searchFields]);` â€” searchFields is included as a dep, but the convention in this codebase is to call useTableControls with an inline literal: e.g. `useTableControls(rows, { searchFields: ['dcfg_name', 'dcfg_status'] })`. Inline arrays are recreated on every parent render, so React identity-checks the array reference and the useMemo cache is invalidated every render. The expensive sort+filter then re-runs on EVERY parent re-render â€” defeating the entire purpose of useMemo. This is the highest-leverage performance finding in the shared modules: 6 separate consumers (MsaList, ContractList, CustomerList, Locations, ViewSmartList, CustomerList) each pay this cost on every keystroke and every state update.
evidence: useTableControls.jsx:14 default param `searchFields = []`, useTableControls.jsx:63 deps array includes searchFields. Grep across src for `searchFields:\s*\[` finds 6 callers: MsaList.jsx, contracts/ViewSmartList.jsx, screens/ContractList.jsx, screens/CustomerList.jsx, screens/Locations.jsx, useTableControls.jsx (the default).
recommendedFix: Two-part: (1) In useTableControls.jsx, hash the searchFields array into a stable string key for the deps: `const searchFieldsKey = (searchFields || []).join('|'); const filtered = useMemo(() => {...}, [rows, sortCol, sortDir, searchTerm, searchFieldsKey]);` This is the smallest change and fixes the cache for every consumer at once without forcing them to refactor. (2) Optionally add a comment block at the top of useTableControls.jsx documenting that callers can safely pass inline literals (because the hook now handles it internally).

title: PortalUserProvider value object created without useMemo â€” context consumers re-render on every provider render

In practice the provider only re-renders when its own state (user, loading) changes, so this is rarely an issue, but if a parent ever re-renders the provider (e.g., a future routing change), every child that calls usePortalUser() will re-render unnecessarily. title: CREATE_ACTIONS references <NewContractIcon /> JSX before the function is declared
detail: Line 25-31 declares CREATE_ACTIONS as a module-top-level constant containing JSX expressions like `icon: <NewContractIcon />`. The NewContractIcon function is defined at line 644, AFTER this constant. Function declarations are hoisted in JavaScript so this works at runtime by accident â€” but it's brittle and hostile to readers, especially because every action uses the SAME icon (<NewContractIcon />) which is also wrong UX (per the spec, four create actions should have distinguishable icons). Linting/formatter passes that re-order code or strict-mode bundlers could break this. Plus the duplicated icons are a UX issue: 'Proposal', 'Vendor Agreement', 'Work Order', 'Amendment', 'Project' all show the same icon in the create zone.
evidence: NavPanel.jsx:25-31 CREATE_ACTIONS array, NavPanel.jsx:644 `function NewContractIcon()` â€” declared 619 lines later.
recommendedFix: Two-part: (1) Move all icon function declarations ABOVE the CREATE_ACTIONS / NAV_GROUPS constants so the dependency order is explicit. (2) Add distinct icons for the four action types â€” at least swap to a 'plus over rectangle' for Project, 'edit' for Amendment, etc. UX polish but worth it for first-impression external testing.

title: External nav item to=/concierge has no live route â€” broken link if config returns nothing
detail: Lines 80-81 declare nav items with `externalFn: () => getEnvVar('concierge_portal_url')` and `externalFn: () => getEnvVar('customer_portal_url')`. If the config row is missing, externalFn returns null, which means NavItem at line 355 evaluates `externalUrl = item.external || (item.externalFn && item.externalFn())` to null, which falls through the `if (externalUrl)` branch and renders a NavLink to=/concierge â€” which has NO matching Route in AppRouter.jsx (concierge isn't in the route list). So a user clicks 'Concierge Onboarding Website' and lands on the NotFound page. Same for /portal.
evidence: NavPanel.jsx:80 `{ to: '/concierge', label: 'Concierge Onboarding Website', icon: <CustomersIcon />, externalFn: () => getEnvVar('concierge_portal_url') }`. AppRouter.jsx:56-151 has no /concierge or /portal route.
recommendedFix: When externalFn returns null/empty, hide the nav item entirely (return false from isVisible). Add a check in isVisible: `if (item.externalFn && !item.externalFn()) return false;`. Optional: add a tiny 'Configure URL' indicator for admins so they know the row needs to be set in dcfg_configs. Coupled with CR-2026-04-09-0211 (config race) â€” until config loads, externalFn returns null and the item is hidden, which is acceptable.

title: NavPanel re-runs filter on every render â€” visibleItems/visibleActions not memoized
detail: Line 159-180 â€” `CREATE_ACTIONS.filter(a => isVisible(a))` and `group.items.filter(isVisible)` run on every NavPanel render. Each call walks the dcfg_configs lookups via getEnvVar and the role-helper checks. Not catastrophic (NavPanel re-renders only on portal user resolve and config-changed events), but `isVisible` references `user`, `getEnvVar`, and the role helpers â€” making it hard to memoize cleanly. Catalog as P3 polish; useMemo would help if NavPanel becomes a re-render hot spot under future routing changes.
evidence: NavPanel.jsx:159-180 â€” filter calls in render body.
recommendedFix: Wrap the visible-actions and visible-groups computation in useMemo with deps `[user, collapsedGroups]` (assuming getEnvVar reads from a stable cache). Low priority â€” NavPanel doesn't currently re-render frequently.

title: isVisible early-returns true for /admin â€” admins can never lock themselves out, but neither can anyone else
detail: Line 124: `if (item.to === '/admin') return true;` â€” the comment above it (line 122) says 'System Admin is always visible (can\'t lock yourself out)', which is reasonable policy for ADMIN users. But the implementation makes /admin always visible to ALL users including viewers. Combined with CR-2026-04-09-0219 (no router-level RoleGuard), this is the smoking gun: viewer roles see /admin in the nav, click it, and get the full Admin screen. P2 because operator may have intended this short-term, but it must be removed before external testing.
evidence: NavPanel.jsx:122-124 â€” comment 'System Admin is always visible (can\'t lock yourself out)' followed by `if (item.to === '/admin') return true;`
recommendedFix: Replace with role-aware check: `if (item.to === '/admin') return isAdmin();`. Combined with CR-2026-04-09-0219 router guard. If the operator wants admins to never be locked out by config, the right place is in the role check (admin sees admin even if config disables it), NOT in the override path that also unlocks viewers.
rejectReason: Duplicate of CR-2026-04-09-0220 (batch 01). NavPanel isVisible was replaced with return isAdmin() in batch 01 at SPA commit 39f8efb. No separate fix needed.

title: RoleGuard component is correct but has zero call sites in shared modules â€” never wired into the router
detail: RoleGuard.jsx is well-built: it consults usePortalUser, returns null on loading, returns fallback on deny, returns children on allow. The C-06 rule (suppress, never disable) is correctly implemented. The problem is that RoleGuard is essentially dead code â€” it isn't imported in App.jsx, AppRouter.jsx, NavPanel.jsx, or any other shared module. The intended consumers (admin actions like Void Contract, Generate Document) live in screen files outside the Phase 1 scope, and the routes themselves don't use it (CR-2026-04-09-0219). File-level finding rather than line-level because the issue is the lack of usage, not anything wrong inside the file.
evidence: Grep across src/ for `RoleGuard` finds: definition in src/RoleGuard.jsx and zero imports in shared modules. Shared modules audited: main, App, AppRouter, portalApi, useTableControls, usePortalUser, Toast, NavPanel, RoleGuard, SlideOutPanel, SpeechMic, FieldName, ErrorReporter, LocationManager, SensorBanner, intakeFieldKeys, projectConstants â€” none import RoleGuard.
recommendedFix: Apply RoleGuard wherever role gating is needed. Highest-leverage application is in AppRouter.jsx around the admin/internal routes (see CR-2026-04-09-0219). Phase 3 screen audit will find more action-button gating opportunities (e.g., Void Contract button). Phase 1 fix batch should include RoleGuard imports in AppRouter.jsx + the admin routes wrapped.

title: useCallback onMouseDown depends on `width` â€” recreated on every drag tick
detail: Line 31-38: `var onMouseDown = useCallback(function(e) { ... startW.current = width; ... }, [width]);` â€” width changes on every mousemove event during a drag, which means useCallback is invalidated on every drag tick and the React reconciliation may discard memoization further down. The fix is to read width via a ref instead of the closed-over variable: keep a `widthRef.current = width;` ref alongside the state, and read `startW.current = widthRef.current;` inside an empty-deps useCallback. Standard React refs-for-fast-changing-state pattern.
evidence: SlideOutPanel.jsx:31-38 useCallback with [width] dep; SlideOutPanel.jsx:46 setWidth fires on every mousemove.
recommendedFix: Add a ref `var widthRef = useRef(width);` at the top, sync it via `useEffect(() => { widthRef.current = width; }, [width]);`, then change useCallback deps to `[]` and read `widthRef.current` inside. Smaller GC pressure during drags. P2 because the drag is short and human-paced â€” only matters if a future Phase 3 finding cites slide-out perf.

title: localStorage.setItem wrapped in try/catch with empty handler
detail: Lines 24, 53, 108-109 (this file and similar in NavPanel/Toast) all wrap localStorage access in `try { ... } catch(e) {}`. localStorage CAN throw (Safari private mode, quota exceeded, disabled storage). The current behavior â€” silently fall back to in-memory state â€” is reasonable. P3 polish: a one-time console.warn would help diagnose 'why doesn't my saved width persist'.
evidence: SlideOutPanel.jsx:53 `try { localStorage.setItem('dcfg_panel_width_' + testId, String(width)); } catch(e) {}`
recommendedFix: Add a one-time guard: `if (!_dcfgLocalStorageWarned) { console.warn('[DCFG] localStorage unavailable â€” UI preferences will not persist'); _dcfgLocalStorageWarned = true; }` inside the catch. Optional polish; not blocking.

title: rec.onerror handler discards the error event entirely
detail: Line 40: `rec.onerror = () => setListening(false);` â€” the SpeechRecognition error event includes an `error` property (e.g. 'no-speech', 'not-allowed', 'network') that would be useful diagnostic info. The current handler just stops the spinner and the user sees no feedback. For Safari/iOS users denying mic permission, they get nothing. Low priority because the feature is optional, but worth surfacing.
evidence: SpeechMic.jsx:40 `rec.onerror = () => setListening(false);`
recommendedFix: Capture the error: `rec.onerror = (e) => { setListening(false); console.warn('[SpeechMic] error:', e.error); };`. Optionally, if onTranscript caller wants to know, add an `onError` prop. Don't toast â€” that would be annoying for accidental clicks. Just diagnose-via-console for now.

title: FieldName visibility relies on bg prop â€” defaults to '#fff', which fails over non-white backgrounds
detail: Line 17 default: `bg = '#fff'`. The visibility trick is to set the field-name span color to match the parent background, so the schema name is invisible until highlight or debug. This works perfectly when the parent IS white, but fails over the navy nav (#1B2A4A), grey card backgrounds, amber callouts, etc. â€” the schema name shows as a white smudge. There is a separate FnTh wrapper for table headers that defaults to #1B2A4A, but no equivalent for navy banners or amber pills. Many call sites just call <Fn> with no bg and end up with visible '#fff' on non-white parents. Per feedback_field_names_invisible.md the contract is 'invisible until highlight'.
evidence: FieldName.jsx:17 default `bg = '#fff'`. LocationManager.jsx:947, 957, 959, 963, 975 calls <Fn f="..."> on a steel-coloured background â€” defaults to white, becomes a visible smudge. Same in NavPanel sections.
recommendedFix: Either: (1) replace default with a CSS variable so it inherits parent background via `currentColor`-style trick (requires parent CSS variable wiring), or (2) add a contextual wrapper convention â€” every screen that uses non-white backgrounds passes the explicit bg prop. Option 1 is harder (would need design pass), option 2 is mechanical (Phase 3 wave will catch each screen one by one). Phase 1 finding only â€” log it and let Phase 3 audit each screen. No fix in this batch.

title: alert() fallback when audit log fails â€” modal alert disrupts external tester flow
detail: Line 75: `alert('Could not send report. Please use Win+Shift+S to screenshot the issue and send to Joseph via Teams.');` â€” Native alert() blocks the page until dismissed. For an external customer tester this is jarring and the message references Joseph + Teams (internal-only context). Should be replaced with the existing Toast component.

The Win+Shift+S tip is internal triage and shouldn't be exposed to external testers. Drop the Joseph/Teams reference entirely from the customer-facing build.

title: userName prop default 'unknown' â€” same upstream usePortalUser gap as LocationManager
detail: Line 16: `var userName = props.userName || 'unknown';` â€” caller must pass userName. NoraCopilot embeds ErrorReporter and passes `userName={user?.email || user?.name || 'unknown'}` (App.jsx:313). Works, but couples the caller to knowing the user shape. title: APPL_COLS referenced but never defined â€” ReferenceError on every openLocation()
detail: Line 473 builds the appliances $select clause via template literal `?$select=${APPL_COLS}&$expand=...`, but APPL_COLS is never defined or imported anywhere in the file. The first time a user taps a location in the field-ops view, openLocation() runs Promise.allSettled with this URL and the apiGet call will throw `ReferenceError: APPL_COLS is not defined` at the URL-build step (before the network call even fires). Promise.allSettled swallows it as a rejected entry, so the appliances state silently stays empty and no toast surfaces â€” the appliance grid will appear blank and the user has no idea why. Hard breakage of the entire field-ops appliance flow.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:473 â€” `apiGet(`/${EntitySets.appliances}?$select=${APPL_COLS}&$expand=dcfg_appliance_type_id($select=dcfg_name,dcfg_icon,dcfg_expected_lifespan_years)&$filter=_dcfg_property_id_value eq ${propertyId} and dcfg_is_active eq true&$orderby=dcfg_location_in_property asc`)`. Grep across LocationManager.jsx finds APPL_COLS only on this single line; no const/let/var/import declares it.
recommendedFix: Define an APPL_COLS constant near the DETAIL_COLS block (lines 53-64) listing every appliance column read by normaliseAppl() at line 146-162: `const APPL_COLS = 'dcfg_applianceid,dcfg_custom_label,dcfg_brand,dcfg_location_in_property,dcfg_install_date,dcfg_serial_number,dcfg_primary_photo_url,dcfg_serial_photo_url,dcfg_replace_by_status,dcfg_estimated_replace_by';` Verify by tapping any property in the field-ops view (`/#/field`) on Test and confirming the appliance list loads without console errors. Cross-check the column list against the 4 explicit-list table rule â€” dcfg_appliances is NOT in the 4 explicit-list tables on Prod, so wildcard would also work, but explicit $select is still preferred per pick-lane discipline.

title: apiPost called with 3rd arg + treated as if it returns the created record
detail: Line 555: `const created = await apiPost(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body, true);` â€” the third argument `true` is silently ignored because apiPost in portalApi.js (line 159) only accepts (path, body) and returns nothing (it does `if (!resp.ok) throw â€¦` then falls off the bottom with no return statement). The very next line tries to read `created?.dcfg_applianceid`, which is always undefined, so the new appliance card created in setAppliances at line 563 always has id/guid = undefined. Subsequent debounced PATCH attempts keyed off that undefined GUID will fail or no-op. Photo upload at line 559 also passes undefined as the appliance_id. The author clearly intended apiPostReturn (which returns the created record).
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:555-556: `const created = await apiPost(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body, true); const newGuid = created?.dcfg_applianceid;` portalApi.js:159 `export async function apiPost(path, body) { ... }` (no return statement, no third param).
recommendedFix: Replace `apiPost` with `apiPostReturn` (already imported pattern in portalApi.js for tables that need the created record back) and drop the spurious `true` arg: `const created = await apiPostReturn(`/${EntitySets.appliances}`, body); const newGuid = created?.dcfg_applianceid;` Then verify by adding an appliance via the field-ops view and confirming the new card has a real GUID (visible in subsequent PATCH calls in network tab).

title: userName destructured from usePortalUser() but no such property exists
detail: Line 354: `const { userEmail, userName } = usePortalUser();`. usePortalUser returns the context shape from PortalUserContext, which exposes `user`, `loading`, `hasRole`, `isAdmin`, `isManager`, `isViewer`, `userEmail` â€” but NOT `userName`. (The user's display name lives at `user.name`.) As a result, every reference to `userName` in this file resolves to undefined: line 1099 `userName?.split(' ').map(...)` always falls back to 'FT' avatar initials and the avatar is always wrong for the field-ops user.

LocationManager.jsx:1099 `userName?.split(' ').map(w => w[0]).join('').slice(0, 2) || 'FT'`
recommendedFix: Change destructure to pull the user object and read `user?.name`: `const { user, userEmail } = usePortalUser(); const userName = user?.name;` (and update line 1099 reference to use that local). Alternatively, expose `userName` from usePortalUser directly to mirror userEmail â€” but that requires a small portalUser change and is the broader fix; LocationManager-only fix is the safer Phase 5 option.

title: Hardcoded /dcfg_properties() entity-set string in @odata.bind instead of EntitySets.properties
detail: Lines 498 and 544 hardcode the string `/dcfg_properties(...)` for the dcfg_property_id@odata.bind value, while every other reference in this file uses `${EntitySets.properties}`. Also breaks the grep pattern that searches for EntitySets.properties to find all consumers.

recommendedFix: Replace both with `'dcfg_property_id@odata.bind': `/${EntitySets.properties}(${currentPropertyId})``. EntitySets is already imported at line 28. Mechanical, low-risk change.

title: uploadPhoto silently swallows getEnvVar and fetch errors
detail: uploadPhoto() (lines 182-197) wraps both the env-var lookup and the fetch in catch blocks that return the dataUrl as-is â€” meaning on a real failure (Power Automate down, flow URL not configured) the user sees the photo persist in-memory and a toast 'Photo saved' (line 604) but the photo is NEVER saved to SharePoint or Dataverse. Reload the page and the photo is gone. This is the #1 silent-data-loss pattern in field ops.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:182-197 â€” both `try { flowUrl = await getEnvVar('dcfg_flow_appliance_photo_url'); } catch { /* */ }` and the inner `try { ... } catch { return dataUrl; }` swallow errors. Line 604: `toast.show('ok', 'ðŸ“· Photo saved');` runs even if upload silently failed.
recommendedFix: Surface failures via toast: change `catch { return dataUrl; }` to `catch (e) { console.warn('uploadPhoto failed:', e); throw new Error('Photo upload failed â€” check connection'); }` and update handlePrimaryPhoto/handleSerialPhoto callers to await + try/catch + toast.show('err', 'Photo not saved â€” try again') on rejection. Also surface 'photo URL not configured' if getEnvVar returns null after config has loaded (don't fall back silently).

title: apiPatch .catch(() => {}) on appliance photo URL save swallows errors silently
detail: Lines 602 and 613: after uploading a primary or serial photo, the code patches the appliance row with the new URL using `.catch(() => {})` â€” discarding any 4xx/5xx error from Dataverse. If the Webapi/dcfg_appliances/fields list ever drifts and dcfg_primary_photo_url / dcfg_serial_photo_url are missing, the toast still says 'Photo saved' but the URL never persisted, leading to silent data loss.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:602 `if (a.guid) await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.appliances}(${a.guid})`, { dcfg_primary_photo_url: url }).catch(() => {});` and :613 same pattern for dcfg_serial_photo_url.
recommendedFix: Replace `.catch(() => {})` with `.catch(e => { console.error('Photo URL save failed:', e); toast.show('err', 'Photo uploaded but link could not be saved â€” refresh and retry'); })`. Same fix at both lines.

title: loadCustomers / openCustomer console.warn-only error handling
detail: Both loadCustomers (line 438-446) and openCustomer (line 448-462) catch errors with `console.warn(...)` only â€” no user-facing toast. The user sees an empty customer list or empty location list with no idea whether the data is empty or the API failed. In the field-ops mobile context this is especially confusing because the network can drop mid-session.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:445 `} catch (e) { console.warn('Customer load failed:', e.message); }` and :460 `} catch (e) { console.warn('Location load failed:', e.message); }`
recommendedFix: Replace both warns with toast surface: `} catch (e) { console.warn('Customer load failed:', e); toast.show('err', 'Could not load customers â€” check connection'); }` (toast is already imported at line 32). Same fix for openCustomer's location-load catch.

title: updateApplField runs Array.find on appliances array on every keystroke
detail: updateApplField (line 520-533) does `appliances.find(x => x.id === id)` after the optimistic setAppliances. This happens on EVERY keystroke into the appliance text fields (custom_label, brand, location, install_date, serial). For a property with 20 appliances that's 20 lookups per character typed. Not a perf catastrophe but combines with the debounced setTimeout to make the data flow harder to reason about. Bonus issue: the closure reads `appliances` from the render snapshot, so it sees the OLD array (pre-update) â€” the optimistic update is one step ahead of the lookup.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:520-533 â€” `setAppliances(prev => prev.map(...)); const a = appliances.find(x => x.id === id);` â€” note that `appliances` is the captured stale array, not the just-updated one.
recommendedFix: Use the value from the prev callback: `setAppliances(prev => { const updated = prev.map(...); return updated; });` Then derive the GUID from `id` directly (since the parameter IS the appliance id) and patch: `if (!dvCol || !id) return;` (the .guid lookup is unnecessary since id === guid throughout this file). Reduces to a simple O(1) flow.

title: Two separate useEffects with [] deps for appliance types and customer list â€” could be parallelized
detail: Lines 416 (load appliance type catalog) and 434 (load customer list) both fire on mount as independent effects. They could be parallelized in a single effect with Promise.all to shave one round-trip on cold load. Minor performance polish.
evidence: LocationManager.jsx:416-431 effect 1, :434-436 effect 2
recommendedFix: Combine into one mount effect: `useEffect(() => { (async () => { await Promise.all([loadApplianceTypes(), loadCustomers()]); })(); }, []);` Low priority â€” only matters on first paint of the field-ops view.

title: sensor_enabled kill switch reads getEnvVar synchronously at top of render â€” race with loadConfig
detail: Line 32: `if (getEnvVar('sensor_enabled') === 'false') return null;` â€” runs at the top of every SensorBanner render, BEFORE the component declares any hooks. Two issues: (1) calling `return` before any hook is illegal in React (conditional hook order). The current early-return happens before useState is reached, so on the FIRST render the component returns null and never registers its hooks. The SECOND render (after config loads and a parent re-renders) it returns the full hooked path, which then crashes with 'rendered fewer hooks than expected' or 'rendered more hooks than expected'. This is the React rules-of-hooks violation. (2) Even ignoring the hook-order bug, getEnvVar returns null on first render before loadConfig resolves (see CR-2026-04-09-0211), so the kill switch never engages on first paint.
evidence: SensorBanner.jsx:30-33 â€” `export default function SensorBanner() { if (getEnvVar('sensor_enabled') === 'false') return null; const [alerts, setAlerts] = useState([]); ... }`
recommendedFix: Move the kill switch check INSIDE a useEffect (or after all hooks are declared). Read it at render time but declare the hooks unconditionally first: `const [alerts, setAlerts] = useState([]); ...all other hooks... if (getEnvVar('sensor_enabled') === 'false' || alerts.length === 0) return null;`. Also subscribe to the dcfg-config-changed event so the kill switch responds to runtime config changes (parallel to NavPanel.jsx:99). Critical to fix before external testing â€” the current hook-order behavior is undefined and could throw at any time.

title: Property lookup interpolates dcfg_location_id_text into a guid filter without quoting
detail: Line 72: `?$filter=dcfg_propertyid eq ${rd.dcfg_location_id_text}` â€” dcfg_propertyid is a GUID column. OData GUID literals don't need quotes (Dataverse accepts both raw and 'quoted' forms), so this works IF the text field actually contains a valid GUID. If the sensor sends any non-GUID value (e.g. a friendly device name like 'GroupHome-12'), the filter generates `eq GroupHome-12` which throws a 400. The catch block at line 79 swallows it and the location name falls back to 'Unknown Location' â€” so the user-visible behavior is 'name not enriched' rather than a hard crash, but the per-alert lookup runs and fails for every reading. Wasteful and brittle.
evidence: SensorBanner.jsx:71-78 â€” apiGet for properties with raw text interpolation; catch on line 79 swallows.
recommendedFix: Validate that dcfg_location_id_text matches a GUID regex before issuing the filter: `if (/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i.test(rd.dcfg_location_id_text))` then run the lookup; otherwise skip enrichment. Saves N round-trips per poll for non-GUID device IDs.

title: Top-level fetchAlerts catch is a bare `catch {}` â€” silent on every poll
detail: Lines 84-86: `} catch { /* Sensor readings table may not exist yet â€” fail silently */ }` â€” every 30s if anything goes wrong (network blip, table moved, response shape changed) we get nothing. Combined with the inner catch on line 79 that already handles 'table not available', the outer catch is a second silent layer that hides post-deploy regressions. P3 because the feature is non-critical, but a one-time warn would help.
evidence: SensorBanner.jsx:84-86 â€” bare catch in fetchAlerts.
recommendedFix: Replace with `} catch (e) { if (!_sensorErrorWarned) { console.warn('[SensorBanner] poll failed:', e); _sensorErrorWarned = true; } }` (using a module-level flag to log only once). Doesn't toast â€” sensor banner is non-critical â€” but gives the developer a breadcrumb.

title: TemplateSection.removeTemplate clears customer lookup with `dcfg_customer_id: null` â€” wrong payload shape
detail: Line 2104: `await apiPatch(`/${EntitySets.docTemplates}(${tplId})`, { dcfg_customer_id: null });` â€” this will not clear the customer lookup. To null a Dataverse lookup via Power Pages you must either PATCH with `{ 'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null }` (same bind-name form the code uses to set it on line 2091) or DELETE the `/entity(id)/dcfg_customer_id/$ref`. Sending `dcfg_customer_id: null` as a plain property either throws 400 or is silently ignored. TemplateDetail.jsx line 641 uses the correct `'dcfg_customer_id@odata.bind': null` form. Net effect on the Admin â†’ Customer Config â†’ Custom Templates tab: 'Remove' button appears to succeed but the template stays linked to the customer.

title: TRADE_OPTIONS constant declared inside CostCodeForm â€” re-created on every render
detail: Line 891: `const TRADE_OPTIONS = [ ... ];` is declared inside the CostCodeForm component body, so a new array and 13 new option-objects are allocated every time the form re-renders. Not a performance hot path (form is short-lived) but the pattern is inconsistent with the module-level SECTIONS/NAV_ROUTES constants at the top of the file. Low priority.

title: DocumentTemplatesTab load + save errors only console.error â€” no user feedback
detail: Line 206 `catch (e) { console.error('Load templates:', e); }` and line 229 `catch (e) { console.error('Save template:', e); }` â€” same pattern repeats for OnboardingStepsTab (424, 447), LocationTypesTab (667, 688), CostCodesTab (802, 823), ApplianceTypesTab (977, 998), VendorsTab (1136, 1157), and IntakeFieldsTab (1587, 1631). title: MsaDetail initial load fetches dcfg_document_url but MSA documents use dcfg_output_file_url

title: OverviewTab builds dynamic OData filter with OR clauses for every MSA ID — potential URL length explosion

title: View switcher buttons lack aria-pressed or aria-current — active state not conveyed to assistive tech

title: Loading skeleton is a plain gray box with no aria feedback — user unaware content is loading

title: Modal overlay has no focus trap and no Escape-key dismiss — keyboard users are stranded

title: writeAuditLog failure in commitTransition is silently swallowed — audit gap invisible
detail: Line 102: `writeAuditLog({...}).catch(e => console.warn('Audit write failed:', e));` — if the audit log write fails after a successful status transition, the only signal is a console.warn. The user sees 'success' but the audit trail has a gap. For a compliance-sensitive contract workflow (Bancroft/SOX), a missing audit log entry could be material. The status change itself is already committed, so this is about observability not data integrity.

detail:
Line 146: `if (loading) return

title: Generate Document button shows 'Generating...' text but is not visually styled as disabled state

detail: Line 71: the document link renders emoji character (page-facing-up) as its visible text content. title: Pagination renders ALL page number buttons at once — 20+ pages renders 20+ DOM buttons
detail: Lines 113-127: the pagination loop iterates from 1 to totalPages and renders a button for each. At PAGE_SIZE=50, a 1000-contract dataset (which hits the client-side cap) means 20 page buttons. title: Expandable table rows use onClick but no keyboard interaction — cannot expand with Enter/Space
detail: Lines 86-100: each contract row has onClick to toggle expansion, but there is no tabIndex, onKeyDown, role='button', or aria-expanded attribute. Keyboard-only users cannot tab to a row or press Enter/Space to expand it. The expand/collapse chevron is visual-only (Unicode triangle).

title: useEffect syncing open-state creates new object every time grouped changes — triggers re-render cascade
detail: Lines 49-55: the useEffect watches [grouped] and calls setOpen(next) where next is a newly constructed object. Because grouped is recalculated by useMemo in useContractData on every page/filter change, this effect fires on every page turn, creating a new open-state object and triggering a full re-render of all customer group headers and their children. With 15+ customer groups visible, this is noticeable as a layout flash.
evidence: ViewCustomerGroups.jsx:49-55 — useEffect([grouped]) sets new open state object unconditionally.
recommendedFix: Use a functional update that only adds new keys without replacing existing ones: setOpen(prev => { var next = {...prev}; grouped.forEach(g => { if (next[g.id] === undefined) next[g.id] = true; }); return next; }). This avoids triggering re-render when the open state hasn't actually changed for existing groups.

title: Pagination uses arrow characters and different styling than ViewSmartList pagination

title: doSearch catch swallows errors silently — search failure shows no feedback to user

title: doSearch builds OData filter with user input but only escapes single quotes — no protection against OData injection

title: Split panel search input has no label or aria-label — same accessibility gap as ContractsList search
